questions.questionText: hour Additional Materials: Multiple Choice Answer Sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) READ THESE INSTRUCTIONS FIRST Write in soft pencil. Do not use staples, paper clips, highlighters, glue or correction fluid. Write your name, Centre number and candidate number on the Answer Sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any rough working should be done in this booklet.
What distinguishes capital from other factors of production?

options.A: Capital exists only in capitalist market economies.
options.B: Capital results from the operation of the other factors.
options.C: The rewards earned by the owners of capital are uncertain.
options.D: Unlike labour or land, capital must be owned rather than hired or rented.

questions.questionText: What is likely to be greater in a planned economy than a market economy?

options.A: efficiency
options.B: flexibility
options.C: innovation
options.D: stability

questions.questionText: Which is a normative statement?

options.A: An increase in the rate of inflation will lead inevitably to an increase in unemployment.
options.B: A reduction in unemployment below a certain level will lead to higher inflation.
options.C: Inflation can be reduced only by increasing the level of unemployment.
options.D: Unemployment is more harmful than inflation.

questions.questionText: What is consistent with an individual demand curve that slopes down from left to right?

options.A: As price falls, a person switches away from rival products towards the product.
options.B: As price falls, a person’s willingness and ability to buy the product will decline.
options.C: As price rises, a person becomes less sensitive to price changes.
options.D: As price rises, a person’s opportunity cost of purchasing the product falls.

questions.questionText: What will cause the demand curve for domestically produced cars to shift to the left?

options.A: an increase in the costs of production of domestically produced cars
options.B: a reduction in taxes on the purchase of cars
options.C: a reduction in the tariff on imported cars
options.D: a reduction in the tax on petrol

questions.questionText: The diagrams show changes in the market for a good.
The diagram shows the demand curve for a product with unitary price elasticity. price D O quantity What will happen with such a curve?

options.A: A fall in price will bring about an increase in expenditure on the product.
options.B: A fall in price will bring about an increase in sales but a fall in expenditure on the product.
options.C: As the price rises, expenditure on the product stays the same.
options.D: As the price rises, expenditure on the product rises and then falls.

questions.questionText: In the diagram D and S are the demand and supply curves of a good. S S price D O quantity What could cause the supply curve to shift in the short run to S ?

options.A: a change in consumer preferences
options.B: a decrease in the price of a complementary good
options.C: a fall in the cost of raw materials
options.D: a government warning that consumption of the good can damage health

The table gives estimates of the price elasticities and cross elasticities of demand for bus and rail travel. elasticity with respect to the price of: service bus travel rail travel bus travel –0.37 +0.13 rail travel +0.16 –0.43 What would be the change in the volume of rail travel resulting from a 1% increase in bus fares?

options.A: an increase of 0.16%
options.B: an increase of 0.43%
options.C: a reduction of 0.13%
options.D: a reduction of 0.37%

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the demand and supply curves for a good. S P P price D O Q Q Q

Global stocks of cod are currently under threat due to over-fishing whilst there are plentiful supplies of the less popular Alaskan pollock. How might the price mechanism operate to limit the depletion of fish stocks?

options.A: The price of both cod and Alaskan pollock will fall.
options.B: The price of both cod and Alaskan pollock will rise.
options.C: The price of cod will fall whilst the price of Alaskan pollock will rise.
options.D: The price of cod will rise whilst the price of Alaskan pollock will fall.

questions.questionText: The table shows some of the costs and benefits at a given level of production of a good. costs $m benefits $m private 80 private 90 social 200 external 100 What is correct at this level of production?

options.A: External benefits exceed external costs.
options.B: Private benefits exceed external costs.
options.C: Private costs exceed social benefits.
options.D: Social costs exceed social benefits.

questions.questionText: The consumption of a good generates external benefits. Its market equilibrium is E. Which diagram shows the change in the equilibrium (E to E ) necessary to reflect the correct value of the good to society?

options.A: B C D S S S S 1 S E E

questions.questionText: What is an advantage, rather than a disadvantage, of cost-benefit analysis in deciding on a government investment project?

options.A: Economic agents place different values on external costs and external benefits.
options.B: Estimates of external costs and external benefits are included.
options.C: Forecasts of future costs and benefits vary over time.
options.D: Miscalculations of the costs are financed by the taxpayer.

questions.questionText: What is a distinguishing feature of a public good that is not found with private goods?

options.A: Consumption depends on the ability to pay.
options.B: It creates negative externalities.
options.C: Its consumption by one consumer can have an effect on other consumers.
options.D: Its consumption by one consumer does not restrict consumption by other consumers.

questions.questionText: In the diagram S and S are the supply curves for an agricultural product in years 1 and 2 respectively. D is the demand curve in years 1 and 2. In year 1 the government purchased an amount necessary to ensure that the price was OP. S S (year 1) (year 2) P price D O WX Y Z quantity The price is held at OP in year 2. How much more must the government buy in year 2 than it bought in year 1?

options.A: WX B XY C XZ D YZ

questions.questionText: Each diagram shows the production possibility curves of two economies, X and Y, which produce food and clothes. In which diagram would both economies benefit by specialising in the good in which they have comparative advantage and trading at an exchange rate of 1 unit of clothes to 1.5 units of food?

options.A: B C D

questions.questionText: An argument against trade protection is that it will increase

options.A: competition for domestic industries.
options.B: domestic price levels.
options.C: opportunities for domestic infant industries.
options.D: the current account deficit.

questions.questionText: A country’s terms of trade currently stands at 150 (base year 2000 = 100). Since 2000 the average price the country has received for its exports has increased by 20%. What has been the change in the average price it has paid for its imports?

A government wishes to present its final balance of payments account. It has calculated the current account balance, the capital account balance and the financial account balance. What additional information is required to complete the task?

options.A: change in foreign currency reserves
options.B: foreign aid
options.C: net errors and omissions
options.D: speculative currency flows

questions.questionText: The table shows inflation rates, unemployment rates and changes in money wage rates between 2008 and 2009 for a number of countries. inflation unemployment money wages country % % % France +0.2 9.4 +3.0 Germany +0.2 8.3 +2.7 UK +1.8 7.8 +2.5 US –0.3 9.4 +2.5 What can be concluded from the table?

options.A: On average, those in employment in the UK had an increase in real incomes.
options.B: The same number of people were unemployed in the US and France.
options.C: The same product would have the same price in France and Germany.
options.D: Unemployment was highest where inflation was highest.

questions.questionText: The diagram compares the inflation rates of Paraguay and Argentina between 1950 and 2005. key Paraguay inflation (%) Argentina 1950 1955 1960 1965 1970 1975 1980 1985 1990 1995 2000 2005 What can be concluded about inflation rates in the two countries in the period 1950 to 2005?

options.A: Argentina’s prices fell rapidly between 1992 and 1995.
options.B: Argentina stabilised its price level between 1973 and 1992.
options.C: Paraguay was always more successful than Argentina at controlling its inflation rate.
options.D: Paraguay was most successful at controlling its inflation rate between 1962 and 1970.

questions.questionText: Over a period of a year, the annual rate of inflation falls from 10% to 6%. Which statement is correct?

options.A: The cost of living has increased.
options.B: The purchasing power of money has increased.
options.C: There has been a reduction in the Retail Price Index.
options.D: The standard of living has increased.

questions.questionText: A Japanese company builds a factory in the UK to supply both the UK market and the market in the rest of Europe. What is likely to be the long-run impact on the UK’s balance of trade in goods and on its current balance? balance of trade current in goods balance

options.A: improve improve
options.B: improve uncertain
options.C: worsen improve
options.D: worsen uncertain

questions.questionText: A country experiences changes in the value of its exports and imports of goods and services and its inflow of incomes and transfers. These are shown in the table. Which set of changes is most likely to cause a depreciation in its floating exchange rate? net inflow of export value import value incomes and transfers

options.A: fall fall fall
options.B: fall rise fall
options.C: rise fall rise
options.D: rise rise rise

questions.questionText: What is likely to happen if there is a rise in the international value of a country’s currency?

options.A: a fall in the foreign currency price of its exports
options.B: a fall in the volume of its exports
options.C: a rise in the domestic currency price of its imports
options.D: a rise in the domestic price level
